status_note: freeze.py sets status, frozen_at_utc and harness_commit and writes FREEZE.json with the SHA-256 of this file, of the schedule and of every code file; run_replication.py refuses a live window, and analyze.py a final status, unless freeze.verify passes. It refuses to freeze without window boundaries, interruption rules, a schedule within the call budget, committed code, or if records exist.
purpose: Live plumbing check on one model; not part of the replication.

contrasts.claim: W1 advantage on the API cell
W2 advantage on the encoding cell

max_in_flight_note: Lane j of a model takes the blocks whose position in the window is j modulo this number, so the requests of one block stay back to back; the six models run in parallel. Two lanes because the retained re-measurements give Kimi-K2.6 a mean of about 2,550 output tokens per request (median 1,747, maximum 8,000): 320 requests in five hours would need about 45 tokens/s sustained with one lane, about 23 with two.

budget.counts: every attempt, retries included, across all windows; a request issued without a saved response counts as max_attempts
budget.note: Raised from 8,192 to fit 40 blocks per window: 11,520 requests leave 768 calls (6.25%) for retries.

request.prompt_suffix: Return ONLY the raw Python file content, no markdown fences, no prose.
request.endpoints: each model's endpoint and key come from its own environment variables; there is no shared fallback; the endpoint is recorded as its provider domain with the resource name hashed, never with the key
request.note: Identical to the published harness: nothing but the model name, one user message and the output-token limit is sent.

retry_policy.exhausted: recorded as a missing observation ('failed'), never as a failed draw, and never requested again
retry_policy.halt: after 3 consecutive failed requests a model stops for the rest of the run, so a dead endpoint or wrong key cannot spend the budget; the window stays open to be fixed and resumed before its end

interruption_rules: A window's requests are issued only from its start to its end; no request is issued at or after the end (the retries of a request issued before the end may finish after it), and a run is started or resumed only inside its window.
Each scheduled request is issued at most once. Its response is saved before it is graded; a saved response is graded on resumption and never requested again.

A request issued but not saved because the run stopped in flight is 'interrupted', and one whose transport attempts are exhausted is 'failed'; both are missing observations and neither is requested again.
Requests not issued by the end of their window are 'not collected'; they are never carried into another window, and the window is closed with --close after its end.
Every attempt, retries included, counts against the global call budget. Once it is spent, no attempt is made in any window, and every remaining window is closed with --close.

A model whose last 3 requests all failed in transport is halted for the rest of the run; its failed requests are not requested again, and the window stays open so the endpoint can be fixed and the window resumed before its end.
A window lost as a whole (an outage, missing credentials) is closed, reported as missing and not replaced.
One run at a time per record directory, guarded by a lock file; after a crash the lock is deleted by hand once no run is active.

The analysis is final only when every planned window is closed, nothing is pending or ungraded, the records match the schedule and the design, and the freeze holds; until then every result is provisional.

grading.primary: published exit-status grader (harness commit 5a5dbcc), run in a credential-stripped environment
grading.deviation: The published grader inherited the parent environment, including provider keys; the replication strips it before running generated code.

analysis.nested_harm_claims: Each harm contrast is tested for any harm and for the 0.30 margin at the same level: the margin null contains the any-harm null, so the pair adds no multiplicity.
analysis.estimand: window-averaged effect over the planned windows
analysis.primary_bound: weighted Hoeffding for independent block differences in [-1, 1]: sqrt(2 ln(1/alpha) sum_w 1/B_w) / W over the W windows with complete blocks, B_w blocks in window w; no identical-distribution assumption
analysis.missing: primary: complete blocks, averaged over the windows that hold them (planned windows without data are listed); sensitivity: every scheduled block of every planned window with each missing outcome imputed against the claim
